summary: A 53-minute month-opening team meeting. Chris Klevan sets June projections week by week with each closer and setter — Andrew at 13 units and just under $50k, Ben ascending to 18 units modelled at 60% upfront cash collected, Kim at units and dials, Kyla at three units and twenty sets a week — then sends Kim and Kyla into a breakout for a setter call review. The remainder is Chris coaching Ben through two recorded discovery calls, on opening state and frame, on getting to the why-now immediately, and on fact-checking prospects' self-reported health. The most consequential passage is Chris reporting an analysis he ran over the weekend of every sales call taken in May, processed through AI, to determine which prospects actually close. His conclusion contradicts the ICP the company states on live calls. The recording ends mid-sentence as the group leaves and Chris asks Andrew to stay for a one-to-one.
notable: Chris's May close-rate analysis directly contradicts the stated ICP. He reports that the prospects who close are 'guys who have the biggest gap ... they literally had an injury, they have tons of weight to lose, they've fallen off, or they had a recent life event', and successful business people who 'have probably 20 to 25 pounds that they still need to lose', and former athletes who let it go. He states explicitly 'it wasn't like the traditional good to great, you know, it wasn't guys going from like an eight to a 10', and that the 8-out-of-10 prospects 'don't close ... very low rate'. The ICP as quoted to prospects says the opposite on both counts.

Chris says the team will change lead targeting on the back of it: 'we are going to try and optimize towards getting more of, like, the other two tiers on the calendar versus the guys that are just already shredded.'

A defined route exists for no-gap prospects and it is Primal University: 'be honest with them. Be like, dude, like, honestly, probably Primal University.' This is the same product that went unmentioned on two of Andrew's calls in this batch where the prospect asked for a lower tier.

June projections and the cash model: Andrew 13 units at just under $50k; Ben 18 units modelled at '60% upfront cash collected' giving roughly $64k. Deposits are being counted as production — Andrew reports his week as 'it's got two deposits'.

Reps are coached to occupy a clinician posture: 'I can kind of like just be in that doctor frame', with the doctor's-office analogy used to justify leading rather than asking — 'They don't ask me, they just freaking tell me what to do. They want to be guided. They want to be led. That's a sign of authority.'

Chris on prospect self-reports: 'people are bullshitters, like crazy, not because they're genuinely trying to get over on you, but because they actually just overestimate how in shape they are', with the remedy being to get them to list nutrition and schedule in detail rather than challenge them directly.

Ben describes using opening small talk to qualify financially without saying so — 'okay, cool, what do you do for work? ... more or less, financially qualifying them in a way' — framed as 'off the record before we get into it'. Chris pushes back on the off-the-record framing but not on the covert qualification.

Training lineage is named: Eli Wilde's surface / action / identity levels, with Chris claiming 'the people who close consistently at like the 40% plus mark ... they're getting to identity level consistently'. Cole Gordon's team was cited in the 29 May meeting.
A prospect on one of Ben's recordings recognised the method in progress: 'he's like, yeah, I do high-ticket sales dude, you don't have to get me all emotional.'

Andrew reports the Wil Saravia outcome live — 'one of the follow-ups messaged me that the budget is out of his option ... as well as the reimbursement of the $100 deposit' — confirming the deposit was refunded.
Andrew is off for several days in week three plus Polish public holidays on the Thursday and Friday, and will work the weekend instead.
